short: Conformer mel predictor plus pretrained vocoder (M06) and data scaling (M03) are standard; GRID/LRW gains hold, but later tests put SVTS at 78-82% WER on LRS3.
position: SVTS [@mira2022svts] changes the synthesis path (M06), a conformer mel predictor before a frozen LibriTTS Parallel WaveGAN, and the training scale (M03), up to 1,556 hours of LRS3 plus VoxCeleb2. Both are standard: a neural vocoder on predicted features is the most common design (49 of 165 studies, pattern match, Appendix), the [concurrent] VCVTS uses the same vocoder [@wang2022vcvts], and the [concurrent] LipSound2 had pre-trained on about 2400 hours of VoxCeleb2 [@qu2022lipsound2]. The GRID-seen and LRW gains hold when the same group re-scores them in a [later] table (2.37% and 12.90% WER) [@kefalas2023large]. The LRS3 claim does not: the paper gives no LRS3 WER, as the authors note, and a [later] test of the authors' own LRS3 files finds 82.4% WER and intelligibility MOS 2.17 [@yemini2024lipvoicer], with 78.0% in a second [later] test [@choi2024v2sflow]. Crediting the gains to scalability is unsupported: model size, data and an audio speaker embedding change together.
